A 65-year-old male is being considered for shoulder arthroplasty. The surgeon is debating between a deltopectoral approach and a superior (anterosuperior) approach. What is one advantage of the deltopectoral approach?
A) Less risk of neurovascular injury
B) Better exposure of the glenoid
C) Reduced postoperative pain
D) Easier access to the humeral head
flags.suggestedAnswer:
B)
The deltopectoral approach is a workhorse internervous approach for shoulder arthroplasty that provides excellent exposure of the glenoid, which is one of its key advantages over superior (anterosuperior/rotator-cuff-sparing) approaches. Superior approaches can limit glenoid visualization and preparation, making glenoid component placement more challenging.

A is incorrect because the deltopectoral approach requires careful identification and protection of neurovascular structures (e.g., axillary nerve, cephalic vein), and it does not inherently carry less risk of neurovascular injury compared to a superior approach.
C is incorrect because the deltopectoral approach involves more soft-tissue dissection including subscapularis takedown, and is not generally associated with reduced postoperative pain compared to less invasive superior approaches.
D is incorrect because both the deltopectoral and superior approaches provide adequate access to the humeral head; this is not a distinguishing advantage of the deltopectoral approach.
